newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures driven higher by gasoline, technical strength.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures driven higher by gasoline, technical strength.

text.p: IPE oil futures closed higher as Brent built on earlier technical strength and took additional support from stronger NYMEX gasoline, brokers said.

Jan Brent closed 13 cents up at $23.75 a barrel. Prices dipped earlier in the day to a low of $23.35 a barrel but recovered after shaking of jitters following remarks by an Iraqi oil official suggesting crude exports were likely to start next week.
"There was technical strength and it just built on that," a broker said, adding there was no fresh news to drive prices higher.
Gas oil was also firmer, having closed $3 a tonne higher at $223 a tonne but it was NYMEX unleaded which pulled both New York and London crudes higher in the afternoon.
The strike at Elf's three refineries has crippled a quarter of French refinery capacity which the U.S. market saw as depriving it of any imported material from Europe.
The American Petroleum Institute is due to release weekly U.S. stock figures with analysts divided as to whether there will be a draw or a build in distillates stocks.
Traders said speculation over the timing of Iraqi crude exports was having little effect on market moves.
"The position that we're taking is that we'll believe it when we see it," said a dealer.
